subject: Alliances: Integration failure-mode workshop & reference design verification
messages:
From: Anne Dubois <anne.dubois@elliotsys.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-20T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: integration flakiness during heavy traffic (preliminary notes)

Hi Sergio / Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick triage earlier this week. We ran the extended load run on Friday night and reproduced a couple of new failure patterns — mostly around partial responses when we cross a 12k token session boundary and occasional 500s from the proxy during KV cache eviction. I've attached a small sample (failure-modes.csv) with timestamps and request ids.

We think this is likely to be a combination of the partner adapter's keepalive semantics and the way Redwood's runtime is falling back to a smaller quantized variant under memory pressure. Before we escalate to our infra teams, would you be open to a short technical workshop next week to walk through failure modes and agree on a verification plan for the reference design?

Proposed outcomes:
- Shared failure catalogue with reproducible steps
- Agreed acceptance criteria for the integration test harness
- Action owners and dates for any adapter fixes or runtime policy tweaks

Availability: Feb 24–25 (PST) best for our engineers.

Thanks,
Anne
Anne Dubois
Platform Lead, Integrations
Elliot Systems

Anne — thanks for the sample and clear summary. Yes, let's do a focused workshop. I've looped in our solution lead (Karthik), QA lead (Mina) and alliances PM (Lauren) so we can walk through the technical root causes and produce a short verification checklist.

Can you confirm whether the failures were seen against your adapter in both our Dedicated and Hosted testbeds? If you only hit it on Dedicated, that points more strongly at the quantized variant selection. If it's both, we need to consider a routing/policy issue.

I'll coordinate an agenda and send a calendar invite for a 90-minute slot. Can you share any additional logs or a minimal repro script before the session?

— Sergio

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Anne Dubois <anne.dubois@elliotsys.com>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-22T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: integration flakiness during heavy traffic (preliminary notes)

Anne — quick technical notes ahead of the workshop: we pulled the sample and identified three candidate vectors to investigate:

1) KV cache eviction threshold mismatch: our runtime will gracefully switch to a quantized runtime when estimated KV memory > X. If your adapter holds long-lived sessions with big prefix context that can push us across the threshold, you can see partial token drops as the kernel swap happens mid-request.

2) Adapter keepalive & retry behaviour: if the adapter retries or replays requests during transient upstream congestion, we can observe duplicate partial responses. We need the adapter's TCP/HTTP keepalive and retry config.

3) Proxy 502/500 path during autoscale: some of the 500s line up with pod churn in Dedicated. We'll check our autoscaler logs during the timestamps you provided.

For the workshop, please include:
- Minimal repro (curl/postman) + request ids
- Attach the adapter's connection config (timeouts, max-connections)
- Any traffic shaping rules you run from your side

We'll prepare a small harness that can toggle the quantized fallback and simulate forced KV eviction so we can reproduce reliably.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

We're available Feb 24 (10:00–12:00 PST) or Feb 25 (13:00–15:00 PST). We'll bring Tom (adapter lead) into the call.

Anne
From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Anne Dubois <anne.dubois@elliotsys.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-24T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Workshop — test harness & acceptance criteria (notes)

Anne / team — draft test plan ahead of today's session (attached as redwood-test-harness-guide.md):
- Controlled run with 1k concurrent sessions, variable prefix sizes up to 16k tokens
- Toggle quantized fallback on/off to observe partial-response delta
- Measure: token success rate, 95th/99th latency, incidence of 5xx per 10k requests
- Acceptance: no partial-response regressions when fallback is disabled; documented mitigation path when fallback is enabled

I'll bring a sandbox that can force KV eviction at pre-set intervals so we can step through reproductions.

— Mina
QA Lead, Redwood Inference
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Anne Dubois <anne.dubois@elliotsys.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-02-28T17:42:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Workshop outcomes & next steps

Great workshop today — thanks everyone for the focused run. Summary / actions: 

- Root cause: KV eviction + adapter keepalive mismatch triggered quantized-fallback mid-request in Dedicated. Confirmed via forced eviction test.
- Short-term: Anne / Elliot to patch adapter keepalive (Tom) to respect longer read-timeouts; ETA 2027-03-07. (Owner: Elliot Systems)
- Medium-term: Karthik / Runtime team to add a guarded kernel-swap window to avoid switching during inflight requests; target PR by 2027-03-14. (Owner: Redwood Runtime)
- QA: Mina to run validation harness against Dedicated nightly for three days post-fix and publish report. (Owner: Redwood QA)
- Documentation: Lauren to update the partner reference design with a new section on session sizing and recommended adapter config. Link to draft: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/alliances/elliot/failure-modes

Attachments recapped: workshop-agenda.pdf, failure-modes.csv, redwood-test-harness-guide.md

If there are any discrepancies in owners/dates above, call them out now and we'll update the action tracker (JIRA PARTNER-4721).

— Sergio
Director, Partnerships & Alliances
Redwood Inference
